rationale: The one fix-set blocking finding (CR-001) is resolved: src/utils/cli-updater.ts:427 now returns true in the sibling-installed branch, the lock is still released in finally, bin/codemie.js relaunches on true, and the child's marker skips the update gate so there is no loop. findings.title: Sibling-installed path skips relaunch
findings.problem: After taking the update lock, getCurrentCliVersion() is compared to the target. If a sibling starter already installed it, the function returns false, so bin/codemie.js does not relaunch. This process still holds modules loaded from the old files while the package files on disk are the new version, so its lazy import of dist/cli/index.js can hit the same 'does not provide an export named' crash this change fixes. The unit test in utils-misc-coverage.test.ts:309-330 pins false for this case and no integration test runs two launchers concurrently.
findings.impact: A concurrent starter that loses the install race still crashes on the first command after an update (acceptance criterion 1: no mixing of cached old modules with new files). Reachability confirmed: the check ran with hasUpdate true against the old installed version, so installed >= target at this point means the files changed under this process.
findings.recommendation: Return true here (the caller relaunches on the new files; the child's marker prevents a loop) and change the unit test to expect true with no install call. Optionally add a fake-npm integration case where the installed version is bumped before the lock.
findings.check_notes: cli-updater.ts:427 returns true in the sibling-installed branch; lock released in finally; codemie.js:99 relaunches on true and the child marker skips the gate (no loop); unit test now expects true.

findings.title: Signal policy double-delivers on mixed TTY setups
findings.problem: signalPolicy() checks only stdin. With non-TTY stdin but a controlling terminal (cmd | codemie), Ctrl+C reaches the child through group delivery and again through the SIGINT forward. With TTY stdin, SIGHUP on terminal close is delivered to the group and also forwarded.
findings.impact: Only the first run after an update with piped stdin (or a closing terminal): the child sees SIGINT or SIGHUP twice, which can force-quit cleanup. Narrow trigger; workaround is to Ctrl+C once more or rerun. Matches the spec's stated policy.
findings.recommendation: Treat the process as foreground when isatty(0), isatty(1) or isatty(2) and ignore SIGINT (and SIGHUP) in that case, forwarding only SIGTERM.

findings.title: relaunch() exceeds 50-line function guideline
findings.problem: relaunch() spans about 72 lines (signal handler setup/teardown, spawn, spawn-error and exit relay) against code-quality.md's 'functions under 50 lines; one responsibility'.
findings.impact: Maintainability only; no behavior consequence. Not enforced by a lint gate, so it does not block.
findings.recommendation: Extract signal handler wiring/teardown and the child exit relay into small helpers so relaunch() stays under 50 lines.

findings.title: Is dropping --inspect* from execArgv intended?
findings.problem: The spec says the child is spawned with process.execArgv, but relaunch() filters out every --inspect* flag so the child does not fail on a taken debugger port.
findings.impact: Behavior is sensible, but the child runs without the debugger flags the user passed; the deviation is not recorded in the spec.
findings.recommendation: Confirm this deviation is intended and note it in the spec, or replay execArgv unchanged.

findings.title: Commit subjects carry the ticket key
findings.problem: Commits e9417435, 860398f5, 858e49b9, dad8838b and 40e7e7c1 all end the subject with (EPMCDME-16837); git-workflow.md Anti-Patterns says to reference the ticket in the body footer instead.
findings.impact: Subject noise only. commitlint does not enforce it and Squash-and-Merge replaces the commit subjects with the PR title, so the trigger is limited to unsquashed history.
findings.recommendation: Move the ticket key to the commit body footer or PR description when squashing; no rewrite needed if the PR is squash-merged.

deferred.title: Launcher continues while another process holds the update lock
deferred.problem: A starter that fails to take the update lock returns false and continues startup while the lock holder may be replacing dist/, so its lazy imports can load half-replaced or mixed-version files.
deferred.preexisting: The lock-held early return predates this change, which relaunches only after this process's own install.

final_round.rationale: All four lenses and the standards audit ran with no gaps. One blocking finding: the post-lock sibling-installed branch returns false and skips the relaunch, leaving the stale-module crash for a losing concurrent starter.
